title: Adaptive Shard Router and Exactly-Once Enrichment for Console Metrics Stream
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Background: Console emits hundreds of different metrics events (route_serve, model_inference, console_action) at variable cardinality. Current ingestion funnels into a single Kafka topic consumed by a fleet of simple processors which do enrichment (add project_id, model_version, route_config) and fan out to downstream stores. We observe hotspots and uneven consumer load during spikes (e.g., model rollouts), consumer rebalances causing visible tail-latency spikes, and duplicate writes when retries happen during partial failures.

Problem: We need a streaming ingress rebuild that: reduces per-event processing latency under burst, adapts routing to changes in key distribution, and guarantees exactly-once writes to our metrics store (time-series + event log) without adding unbounded state or slowing the critical path.

Goals (scope):
- Build an Adaptive Shard Router that assigns events to processor shards by an observable key (project_id or route_id) with fast re-sharding and minimized cross-shard fanout.
- Implement an enrichment service that is horizontally scalable, keeps the enrichment step idempotent, and provides exactly-once semantics for writes to final sinks (ClickHouse for aggregates, S3 event log).
- Keep median end-to-end enrichment+write latency under 120ms at our 99th-percentile load profile and improve 95th/99th tail compared to current baseline.
- Provide migration plan to switch traffic gradually and fall back to the legacy pipeline on regressions.

High-level design:
1) Ingress: events land on topic console.metrics.ingress with a stable event_id (UUID v4) and lightweight headers (project_id, route_id, model_hint). Producers must include event_id - producers will be upgraded in a short follow-up (ENG-15842).
2) Router: a dedicated Router service maintains a sharding table stored in a small Raft-backed config store (existing config-service) and assigns events to shards using a two-pass heuristic: prefer sticky assignment for high-cardinality project_ids, fall back to consistent-hash for low-cardinality keys. The Router writes assignment metadata to a compact assignment topic (router.assignments) to allow consumers to warm caches. Router exposes per-key shard hints for clients to route low-latency directly.
3) Enrichment/Processor: each shard runs a stream processor that performs: schema validation, joins with lightweight in-memory config cache (route metadata), and produces idempotent output records. To achieve exactly-once writes we adopt an at-least-once ingestion guarantee combined with an idempotent sink writer using a deduplication window keyed by event_id stored in CockroachDB (small TTL ~24h) for the event-log write, and for ClickHouse aggregates we use sequence-based upserts with bounded replay safety.
4) Backpressure & buffering: Router will advertise shard capacity; clients will fall back to an internal buffer (bounded) and switch to a secondary low-cost path if short-term overload occurs.

Trade-offs considered:
- True distributed exactly-once (e.g., Kafka transactions) was considered but increases end-to-end latency and couples processors closely to the broker. We chose idempotent sinks + dedupe store to keep processors stateless and allow simpler scaling/failover.
- CockroachDB dedup store introduces operational cost but will only store event_id + shard + write_ts for 24h which is acceptable for our retention SLA.

Acceptance criteria: (see acceptance_criteria list)

Monitoring & observability:
- New dashboards: per-shard latency histogram, Router assignment churn, dedupe-store writes/success rate, end-to-end P50/P95/P99 latency. Dashboards: https://datadog.com/dashboards/console-shard-router and https://datadog.com/dashboards/console-enrichment-latency
- Alerts: abnormal assignment churn (>20% churn in 5m), dedupe-store write error rate >0.1%, P99 latency >450ms.

Migration plan:
- Phase 0: dry-run duplicate writes (processor writes to sinks in dry-run mode) for 24-48h and validate parity against legacy pipeline.
- Phase 1: 5% traffic via Router -> Enrichment, 95% to legacy. Monitor for 48h.
- Phase 2: increase to 25% -> 50% -> 100% once stability confirmed.
- Rollback: Router can remap shards to a passthrough mode that forwards to legacy topic.

Open questions:
- TTL for dedup store (24h provisional) vs cost.
- Producer upgrade strategy (ENG-15842) timeline.

Related artifacts: design doc, benchmarks, and prototype PRs listed below.
acceptance_criteria: Router assigns >95% of high-cardinality project_id events to the same shard for at least 1 hour (measured via assignment topic).
End-to-end median enrichment + write latency < 120ms at 99th-percentile load profile (internal benchmark run).
No more than 0.01% duplicate event_ids observed in final S3 event-log after 7-day sample during dry-run.
Safe rollback path exists and has been exercised during staging cutover.
Operational runbook and dashboard created; on-call knows how to toggle router passthrough and read dedupe-store metrics.
updates: 2026-02-20 - Ticket created by Aisha. Initial design sketched; Router + dedupe store chosen over broker transactions.
2026-02-26 - Design review with Platform and Observability teams: agreed on CockroachDB dedupe-store and Router assignment topic. Action: ENG-15841 to add Router schema to config-service.

2026-03-03 - Prototype: shard router PoC routes synthetic workload; 30% tail latency improvement observed in P99 for enrichment workers. PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3821
2026-03-06 - Integration test harness running against staging Kafka; intermittent dedupe-store contention observed at 3k writes/s — tuning under way (see PR #3839).

2026-03-10 - Code landed for Router service (feature branch). Start running dry-run duplicates on 5% of customer traffic in staging. Monitoring dashboards created: https://datadog.com/dashboards/console-shard-router

2026-03-12 - Early staging results: dedupe-store write p95 = 12ms, router assignment churn 2% over 1h. Proceeding to increase dry-run traffic to 20% pending no regressions. Next: finalize migration playbook and runbook.
